claims.text: Root-cause hypothesis 4.1 (most likely): the Claude Code harness may, by design, restrict sub-agent tool surfaces to a safety-bounded subset, regardless of frontmatter declaration.
claims.notes: §4.1. Analytical claim — root-cause hypothesis. Framer note: may be superseded by T-001 investigation findings.

claims.text: A possible reason for harness restriction is recursion prevention — sub-agents dispatching sub-agents could spawn unbounded chains.
claims.notes: §4.1 first sub-bullet. Analytical claim — sub-hypothesis under §4.1.

claims.text: A possible reason for harness restriction is context-cost containment — each sub-agent dispatch consumes additional tokens; restricting Agent from sub-agents bounds the cost.
claims.notes: §4.1 second sub-bullet. Analytical claim — sub-hypothesis under §4.1.

claims.text: A possible reason for harness restriction is surface-area minimization — sub-agents are intentionally narrower than top-level agents.
claims.notes: §4.1 third sub-bullet. Analytical claim — sub-hypothesis under §4.1.

claims.text: A possible reason for the restriction is an untested code path — the harness may not have ever been used in a pattern that requires sub-agent dispatch.
claims.notes: §4.1 fourth sub-bullet. Analytical claim — sub-hypothesis under §4.1.

claims.text: If harness restriction is the cause, the fix is one of: (a) reading the harness docs to understand the supported pattern and migrating the pipeline to it, (b) modifying agent definitions to not assume Agent dispatch capability, or (c) coordinating with Anthropic on whether sub-agent Agent dispatch is supported.
claims.notes: §4.1 closing. Prescriptive claim — three-way fix option enumeration conditional on hypothesis 4.1.

claims.text: Root-cause hypothesis 4.2 (less likely): the harness might parse the frontmatter tools: array but rewrite it during agent instantiation.
claims.notes: §4.2. Analytical claim — alternate root-cause hypothesis. Framer note: may be superseded by T-001 investigation findings.

claims.text: Frontmatter parsing variation possibilities include: the inline syntax [Read, Glob, Grep, ...] might be normalized differently than the multi-line YAML list form; specific tool names like Agent might be filtered; the Bash(python3:*) scope syntax might be unrecognized and the parser might silently drop the parenthetical.
claims.notes: §4.2 enumeration. Analytical claim — sub-hypotheses under §4.2.

claims.text: The presence of Edit in the runtime surface (despite NOT being in the frontmatter) suggests something more than simple filtering — there is at least some active mutation between declaration and runtime.
claims.notes: §4.2 closing. Analytical claim — load-bearing evidence weighing hypotheses.

claims.text: The Edit-tool evidence weakens the simple-filtering hypothesis and strengthens the active-harness-behavior hypothesis.
claims.notes: §4.2 closing. Analytical claim — interpretive judgment between competing hypotheses.
